meta.titre: Loi Cadre in French Cameroon: how the 1956 reforms created the Legislative Assembly
meta.sous_theme: The Loi Cadre and the Legislative Assembly of French Cameroon
tags: loi cadre reforms in french cameroon

sections.contenu_markdown: In December 1956 voters in French Cameroon went to the polls under rules that were new to them. All adults could vote on one common roll, and the Assembly they chose would meet in Yaounde. The change came from a French law called the Loi Cadre, and it opened the way to internal self-government in 1957. Examiners ask which Assembly appeared, what powers it had and why those powers were limited. This course gives you the sequence and the answer pattern.

items: After 1946 French Cameroon was a United Nations trust territory administered by France.
The UPC was the nationalist party founded in 1948 and it was banned in 1955.
Legislative power means the power to make laws.

sections.titre: The Loi Cadre: what changed, what did not change
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Meaning and background

Loi Cadre means "framework law". The French minister for overseas territories, Gaston Defferre, gave his name to the law of June 1956, which gave more local self-government to French overseas territories. Its principles were then applied to Cameroon, a trust territory. Before this, French Cameroon had elected assemblies with small powers, such as the ARCAM and the ATCAM, and the French High Commissioner held the real authority.

### Main reforms

| Reform | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Universal adult suffrage | All adults could vote |
| One electoral roll | Africans and Europeans voted together, ending separate voting groups |
| New Assembly | The Legislative Assembly of Cameroon, known as ALCAM, was elected in December 1956 |
| Local responsibility | The Assembly could pass laws on local matters |

### Why the Assembly's powers were limited

France kept control of defence, foreign affairs and currency, and the High Commissioner kept final authority. The Assembly handled mainly local questions, so its legislative power was limited. The UPC had been banned in 1955 and did not take part in the 1956 elections.

### Importance

The Loi Cadre gave Cameroonians more experience in government and led to a new statute in 1957 and the first internal self-government. Critics said that real power remained with France. French Cameroon became independent on 1 January 1960.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a short question asks for the name of the Assembly or the law that created it
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give the full name and the short form: the Legislative Assembly of Cameroon (ALCAM), created as a result of the Loi Cadre. Do not give ARCAM or ATCAM, which came before it.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked why the Assembly did not have full legislative power
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give two or three reasons with evidence: defence, foreign affairs and currency stayed with France; the High Commissioner held final authority; the territory was still a trust territory.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the command word is Assess or To what extent
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give gains (vote for all adults, African participation, step to self-government) and limits (France kept key powers, the UPC excluded). Finish with a judgement.

sections.enonce_markdown: Assess the importance of the Loi Cadre reforms for political development in French Cameroon. [8 marks]

etapes.justification: "Assess" asks for a judgement on importance, with points for and against.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Plan a balanced answer ending with a judgement.

etapes.justification: The examiner must see that you know what it was.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A French law of 1956, named after Gaston Defferre, giving more local government to overseas territories and applied to Cameroon.
Universal adult suffrage, one electoral roll, the creation of ALCAM and more Cameroonian experience in government.

etapes.justification: Limits give the second side of an assessment.
etapes.resultat_markdown: France kept defence, foreign affairs and currency; the High Commissioner held final power; the UPC was banned.

etapes.justification: A reasoned verdict earns the top marks.
etapes.resultat_markdown: An important step towards self-government, but not yet real independence.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: The Loi Cadre, a French law of 1956 named after Gaston Defferre, was an important step in French Cameroon. It gave the vote to all adults on one roll and led to the election of the Legislative Assembly (ALCAM) in December 1956, which gave Cameroonians more experience in government and prepared the internal self-government of 1957. However, France kept control of defence, foreign affairs and currency, the High Commissioner held final authority, and the banned UPC took no part in the elections. In conclusion, the reforms were a real step forward but did not yet give independence.

items.erreur_markdown: The Loi Cadre gave French Cameroon independence in 1956.
items.pourquoi_faux: It gave more local power, but France kept key powers. Independence came on 1 January 1960.
items.correction_markdown: Write that the Loi Cadre was a step towards self-government, not independence.

items.erreur_markdown: The Assembly created after the reforms was the ARCAM.
items.pourquoi_faux: ARCAM and ATCAM were earlier assemblies; ALCAM came after the Loi Cadre.
items.correction_markdown: Write ALCAM, the Legislative Assembly of Cameroon.

items.erreur_markdown: The Loi Cadre was passed by the Cameroonian Assembly.
items.pourquoi_faux: It was a French law, extended to the territory.
items.correction_markdown: Say it was a law of the French government.

items.pourquoi_faux: The UPC was banned and did not take part.
items.correction_markdown: Write that the UPC was banned in 1955 and absent from the elections.

items.enonce_markdown: What does the term Loi Cadre mean, and after which French minister is the 1956 law named?
items.solution_markdown: Award a mark for each. **Framework law; Gaston Defferre.**

items.enonce_markdown: Explain two reasons why the powers of the Assembly set up in 1956 were described as limited.
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for two reasons with evidence. France kept defence, foreign affairs and currency. The High Commissioner held final authority. **The Assembly dealt mainly with local matters.**

items.enonce_markdown: To what extent did the Loi Cadre prepare French Cameroon for independence? [10 marks]
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for both sides. Preparation: universal suffrage, ALCAM, more African experience, the 1957 statute and self-government. Limits: key powers stayed with France, the UPC excluded, independence only on 1 January 1960. **Judgement: a stage in a longer process, helpful but not enough by itself.**

items_markdown: Loi Cadre means framework law; the French law of 1956 was linked to Gaston Defferre.
It introduced universal adult suffrage and one electoral roll in French Cameroon.
The Assembly created was ALCAM, elected in December 1956, with limited powers.
France kept defence, foreign affairs, currency and the High Commissioner's final authority.
The UPC was banned and did not take part in the 1956 elections.
The reforms led to internal self-government in 1957; independence came on 1 January 1960.
